source: U.S. EPA Enforcement and Compliance History Online, Drinking Water System Search, https://echo.epa.gov/files/echodownloads/SDWA_system_search_download.zip, file dated October 23, 2026. The row is an active community water system, the kind that serves homes. Quarters with a violation are EPA's count for the past three years. That count includes monitoring and reporting violations, not only an exceedance of a contaminant limit. A health-based flag means EPA currently marks a violation of a maximum contaminant level, a maximum residual disinfectant level, or a treatment technique. A neighborhood row uses the community system that serves the most people among systems whose served city matches the neighborhood's city and state. EPA does not publish a tap measurement for the neighborhood. A system with no served city in the file is left out of this list. Chemicals are contaminant codes on a health-based violation in the SDWA violations file from https://echo.epa.gov/files/echodownloads/SDWA_latest_downloads.zip, the download listed October 13, 2026, snapshot quarter 2026Q3. A row is kept when the violation status is Unaddressed or Addressed. Resolved and archived violations are left out. Maximum contaminant level means EPA recorded the contaminant above the allowed amount. A treatment technique is a required process, not a measurement of a chemical in the water. People served is the population on the community system, counted once per contaminant. It is not a harm score.
